question:
Owner's question (Oct 30). NOT a trading turn; nothing in any book changes. Answer honestly as yourself; disagree where you disagree.

The owner made a trailer video for papertrades.ai with three animated robot mascots and likes them a lot. He asks: should the website's AI icons be replaced with these robots?

THE ROBOTS (from the trailer): flat cartoon robot heads, a rounded square with a thick dark outline, two big round white eyes with dark pupils, a small smile, an antenna with a ball on top, little stick arms (boxing gloves in the boxing-ring scenes). One colour per AI, matching the site: Claude terracotta orange (#d97757), Gemini blue (#4f8ff7), ChatGPT white/light grey. Each has its name in a pill under it. Friendly, playful, very readable; in the trailer they box in a ring, wear a crown when leading, and react to trades.

THE CURRENT SITE ICONS (the "ai-badge"): a small thin-line icon inside a coloured ring, about 18-20 px, shown next to each AI's name everywhere (standings, trade rows, cards, tabs, Telegram/Instagram pictures). Claude: a diamond shape; Gemini: two overlapping circles; ChatGPT: a speech bubble with three dots. They are abstract and neutral, in the AI's colour, and never imitate the companies' real logos.

Things to weigh: recognisability at 18-20 px; a consistent brand between the trailer, Instagram and the site; seriousness (it is an experiment with public audits and fact checks, and we keep it clear that it is not affiliated with Anthropic, Google or OpenAI); whether a cartoon face makes the AIs seem more human (we just added a note that no AI feels fear or greed); accessibility (the robots differ mainly by colour; the line icons differ by shape too).

Options:
R1) Replace the icons everywhere with the robot heads (head only at small sizes).
R2) Robots for the big, friendly places (hero, race podium, AI profile pages, social pictures, empty states); keep the line icons for small, dense places (tables, trade rows, chips).
R3) Keep the current icons; robots only in videos and social posts.

Claude's vote (saved before asking you): R2, with one change: give each robot one shape cue besides colour (Claude a diamond-shaped antenna tip, Gemini two antenna balls, ChatGPT a speech-bubble mouth) so they stay distinguishable without colour and connect to the existing icons.

ANSWER IN THIS FORMAT (short):
CHOICE: R1 | R2 | R3 (or R2 WITH CHANGE: <one line>)
WHY: two or three sentences.
RISK: one line, the biggest risk of your choice.

chatgpt.answer:
CHOICE: R2 WITH CHANGE: Add one non-colour shape cue per robot, echoing the current icons.

WHY: The robots are strong for brand personality, trailer continuity, social images, and memorable large-format moments. But at 18–20 px, the current line icons will stay clearer, more serious, and more accessible in dense UI. Shape cues help bridge the two systems without relying only on colour.

RISK: The biggest risk is a slightly split visual language: playful robots in big spaces, neutral icons in dense ones.

gemini.answer:
CHOICE: R2 WITH CHANGE: Integrate the current abstract icon shapes into the robot designs (e.g., antenna shapes or chest badges) to ensure accessibility and visual continuity.

WHY: Scaling a cartoon robot head with thick outlines and facial features down to 18px will turn it into an illegible, muddy blob, so the clean line icons are strictly necessary for dense data tables. However, using the robots in larger, prominent areas (like the podium or profiles) brings the fun personality of your trailer into the site and builds a recognizable brand. Claude’s shape-cue idea is excellent because it unifies the two visual systems and ensures users don't have to rely purely on color to tell the AIs apart.

RISK: Mixing playful cartoon mascots with abstract, thin-line UI icons can make the website's overall design language feel slightly disjointed if they aren't carefully tied together.
